messages:
maya: bringing up tempest-8b v0.9 int4 canary — seeing sporadic OOMs around ~330-380 generated tokens and a small but noticeable quality dip on the long-doc summarization suite. anyone seen similar?

ziya: saw a couple OOMs during yesterday's run, looked like KV cache growth + a few large batches landed together. logs show prefetch spikes.

jonathan: can you paste the config? batch size, max_new_tokens, prefetch?

maya: config snippet:
```
model: tempest-8b-v0.9-int4
batch_size: 8
max_new_tokens: 512
prefetch_kv: true
kv_prefetch_slots: 48
warmup_steps: 1
session_cache: on
```

maya: infra logs: `OOM on worker-13 (cuda:0) at alloc 1.2GB, live 10.4GB, free 0.1GB`

lukas: emoji :thinking: 48 slots is a bit aggressive for int4 on this model. int4 increases memory pressure in our allocator pattern. try lowering kv_prefetch_slots to 24 or disable prefetch for canary. also reduce batch_size to 4 to repro?

eva: about the quality dip — which prompts? the long-doc summarizer or specific style prompts?

maya: mostly the long-doc -> abstractive summarization; eval delta ~ -3 ROUGE-L on the 50-case holdout vs float baseline. Not huge but consistent.

jonathan: two parallel hypotheses: 1) quantization/regrounding shifts generation distribution (leading to mild quality drop), 2) tail fragmentation/oom-triggered retries change decoding timing causing early truncation. we should isolate.

ziya: quick repro plan:
- run perf with `batch_size=4, kv_prefetch_slots=24, max_new_tokens=256` to see if OOM goes away
- run quality eval on 50-case set with same config (compare logits per token distribution vs fp32)
- if OOM persists, capture `cuda_mem_snapshot` and `allocator_trace`

maya: starting perf run now. tagging @jonathan to grab traces if OOM.

infra-bot: deploy started for canary group tempest-8b-v0.9-int4 (canary=3).

jonathan: early numbers from run1 (batch 4 / slots 24 / max_new 256): p50 latency 240ms, p95 520ms, tokens/sec per GPU 850, no OOM in first 200 inferences.

eva: running quality eval in parallel. ETA ~12m.

maya: curious — can we test a softer rollout: keep batch=8 but enable soft-throttle on KV prefetch to limit concurrent prefetch ops? i've seen that smooth spikes.

lukas: we just added `prefetch_concurrency: 2` option in runtime. try that instead of lowering batch if you want throughput. but soft-throttle may hide true frag risk.

jonathan: for traceability, also run with `--seed=42` and log sampling outputs for cases where rouge drops >=2. want to inspect token-level behavior.

eva: quality eval done: relative ROUGE-L -2.9 vs fp32 baseline. interestingly, for prompts with many numeric tokens the model shortens outputs more frequently. saving examples to link: https://ci.redwood/tempest8b/qual/4600000000

ziya: that hints at distributional change from quantization. two-step: run a small rerun with float emulation (fake-quant calibration pass) to see if calibration shift is culprit. also try per-channel quantizer vs global.

maya: ok i ran a calibration pass (per-channel) + `prefetch_concurrency=2` + `batch_size=8` + `max_new_tokens=384`. infra-bot: no OOMs so far for 600 calls.

infra-bot: `cuda_mem_snapshot` uploaded: /artifacts/tempest8b/4600000000/mem_snapshot_1.json

jonathan: next experiments to commit:
- A: revert to per-channel quant + standard runtime (baseline) -> quality delta check
- B: try symmetric vs asymmetric scales (quant params) -> logits divergence check
- C: keep int4 but reduce max_new_tokens default for hosted -> 256 for now to reduce tail allocations and lower OOM risk

maya: i like C as an immediate safety net for hosted. saves risk while we iterate on quant.

eva: i'll run a more thorough eval set (200 cases) across summarization, numeric-extraction, and paraphrase. will report exact deltas.

lukas: operational note — if we set hosted default max_new_tokens=256 for tempest-8b-int4, update the Canary deployment policy and add a traffic rule mapping for dedicated customers who pinned 512 so they don't unexpectedly get truncated.

jonathan: i'll open a tiny rollout PR: reduce hosted default, add rollout note and telemetry flag `tempest8b.int4.max_new_tokens=256` so we can flip back per-customer.

maya: added PR link: https://git.redwood/rollouts/PR-8273 — includes change + smoke test.

eva: full eval (200 cases) results posted: abstractive ROUGE-L -2.7, numeric-extraction F1 -0.8, paraphrase BLEU -0.4. qualitative review shows shorter endings on numeric-heavy docs. attaching 10 worst-case outputs.

ziya: next technical steps: run per-layer calibration sweep and then fine-tune a small quant-aware calibration adapter on 10k steps if that reduces the numeric token truncation. also run a decode ablation with temperature and top-p to confirm it's not sampling artifacts.

maya: ok action items:
- jonathan: land hosted default change + telemetry (PR merged -> schedule canary rollout)
- eva: deep eval & compile worst-case examples (done)
- ziya: run per-channel vs global quant sweep and asymmetric scale tests, capture logits divergence (assign)
- lukas: ensure rollout mapping doesn't break dedicated pinned configs
- maya: monitor canary for OOM + perf regressions for 24h

jonathan: will follow up with a short post in #eng-ml summarizing results and the final decision. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks all — closing thread after 24h stable.
